label: Zyxel GS1900-8

label: Zyxel GS1900-8HP
description: Zyxel GS1900-8HP - 8x 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ45, all eight PoE+ (802.3at, 30 W/port) against a 77 W budget, fanless desktop smart-managed switch with no SFP.

poe.note: IEEE 802.3at PoE+ on all eight copper ports at up to 30 W per port against a 77 W total budget, so the budget and not the port count is the binding limit: two 30 W PDs plus a third at 17 W already fills it. The user guide LED table numbers these as PoE 10/100/1000Base-T Ports (1 - 8), so every copper port is a PSE port. Default consumption mode powers only what the PD asks for and reserves the remainder; PoE can be scheduled per time range; a PoE MODE button turns the port LEDs into PoE state LEDs.

label: Zyxel GS1900-24EP
description: Zyxel GS1900-24EP - 24x 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ45, 12 of them PoE+ (802.3at, 30 W/port) against a 130 W budget, no SFP cages, smart-managed switch on a smart fan.

poe.note: IEEE 802.3at PoE+ on twelve of the twenty-four copper ports at up to 30 W per port against a 130 W total budget; the other twelve ports carry no power at all. The datasheet states counts only (12 x GbE PoE RJ-45 ports, 12 x GbE RJ-45 ports) and neither the datasheet text layer nor the series user guide names which port numbers form the PSE group, so ports 1-12 are modelled as the PoE group following the model list left-to-right order. That numbering is the one inferred field in this spec; the counts, the standard and the 130 W budget are cited. 130 W cannot fill twelve 30 W ports, so the budget binds before the port count does.
